# Changelog

Notable changes to Pit are documented here. GitHub release notes remain the authoritative detailed record for each tagged release.

## [Unreleased]

## [0.39.1] - 2026-11-19

### Fixed

- OpenAI Codex models that send a `typescript` call as a JSON function call holding the raw program, instead of a grammar call, no longer fail with an argument parse error (#415). Pit recovers the program, including any `// @pit: {...}` options line, before Pi validates and saves the call, so it runs once and replays correctly in later requests. Calls already saved this way in a session are repaired in what Pit sends the model, and the call's row shows the recovered source and label.

## [0.39.0] - 2026-11-18

### Changed

- **Breaking:** Pit supports Pi 1.5.2, the version `package-lock.json` now pins, including `@earendil-works/pi-codemode` 1.5.2, which Pit installs as its own copy. Update Pi to 1.5.2 with this release.
- The runtime dependency audit in CI and the Release workflow skips the withdrawn picomatch advisory GHSA-fc5q-39xc-vjpf (#411).

### Fixed

- A reply that ends with an elided-call record written as text, such as `[Pit: elided tool call: typescript · …]`, and makes no tool call no longer passes silently as a finished action (#409). Nothing ran, so Pit appends a notice for the model and the user, `▲ No tool ran`, and asks the model for one more response to make the call. A reply that repeats the mistake right after the notice gets the notice without another continuation. Elided-call records now end with `already ran; writing this text runs nothing`.

## [0.38.1] - 2026-11-17

### Fixed

- `typescript` calls that set their label or other options in a `// @pit: {...}` source header show that label and those inputs in the call's header and expanded view, as they do when the options are passed as tool arguments. A streaming, malformed, or conflicting header still renders the call as written.
